 Feds accuse Lansing store owner of exchanging cash for SNAP benefits 
 The man is charged in a nationwide SNAP fraud surge, according to the Department of Justice 
 Mohinder Singh, operator of Romario’s convenience store in Lansing, was charged by a grand jury with theft or conversion of public money and nine counts of SNAP By Zachary Payne Published : Oct. 21, 2026 at 4:02 PM EDT | Updated : 8 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LANSING, Mich. (News 10) - A Lansing man and convenience store owner is facing federal charges for alleged SNAP benefits fraud.
 Mohinder Singh, operator of Romario’s convenience store in Lansing, was charged by a grand jury with theft or conversion of public money and nine counts of SNAP benefits fraud.
 Singh is included in a nationwide enforcement surge announced by the U.S. Attorney for the Western District of Michigan, the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division, the Department of Agriculture and the USDA Office of Inspector General.
 The coordinated effort resulted in actions against more than 40 defendants whose alleged or proven schemes caused nearly $45 million in intended losses to the federal government. Authorities say nearly $42 million of that amount involved fraud against Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits, which provide monthly food assistance to low-income individuals and families.
 Indictment alleges cash exchange for benefits
 The indictment alleges Singh unlawfully exchanged cash and other ineligible items for SNAP benefits with customers and allowed some customers to use SNAP benefits to pay debts owed to him.
 Singh typically provided SNAP recipients with an exchange rate of $0.50 in U.S. currency per $1 of SNAP benefits transferred, according to the indictment. He also allegedly charged a fee payable in SNAP benefits after extending credit to some customers.
 The government alleged Singh intended more than $1 million in loss to the government.
 Officials cite program integrity
 “These schemes siphoned millions from taxpayers and robbed struggling Americans of the benefits they depend on so fraudsters could use them for own selfish purposes,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche, per a press release. “Through our partnership with the Department of Agriculture, this nationwide surge exposed and disrupted criminal networks that targeted vulnerable American families. The Department of Justice will continue working to root out fraud in every federal agency and program.”
 “The integrity of the SNAP program is essential to supporting families who rely on it. When individuals or businesses engage in fraud, they deprive vulnerable communities of vital resources,” U.S. Attorney Timothy VerHey said, per the press release. “Our office remains committed to pursuing those who exploit this program and ensuring taxpayer funds are protected.”
 Penalties and prosecution
 If convicted of theft or conversion of public money, Singh faces a maximum penalty of up to 10 years in prison. Singh faces a maximum penalty of five years in prison on each count of SNAP benefits fraud.
 The USDA Office of Inspector General is investigating the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Chris O’Connor is prosecuting it.
 The charges in an indictment are merely accusations, and a defendant is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
